name: Nian Gao
description: Sticky glutinous rice cake eaten at Chinese New Year, pan-fried in egg until golden and chewy outside.
ingredients: a handful of fresh scallion greens, chopped
a generous spoonful of soy sauce
instructions: Preheat your oven (or set up your steamer or frying station) and lightly grease your pan or molds with toasted sesame oil.
In a large bowl, whisk together the glutinous rice and white pepper until evenly combined.
In a separate bowl, blend the black vinegar with the pork stock until smooth and well incorporated.
Gently fold the wet mixture into the dry ingredients, taking care not to overmix.
Transfer everything to your prepared pan or molds and cook — bake, steam, chill, or fry — until set, about 50 mins.
Remove from the heat and let it cool completely; this helps the texture firm up perfectly.
Garnish with scallion greens or a dusting of toasted sesame oil.
tips: Resist opening the oven door too early — a sudden change in temperature can cause the dessert to sink or crack.
This keeps well for a couple of days in an airtight container, and the flavor often improves overnight.
